title: Cold-storage ON/OFF control
physicalPurpose: Regulate cold-room temperature automatically with a compressor that can only be off or on.
objective: Derive a Boolean ON/OFF law, run it on the cold-storage room, measure temperature range and switch count, and explain why one noisy threshold causes chatter.

simplifications: The room and product are represented by one well-mixed thermal state.
The door load changes the no-cooling equilibrium rather than modelling airflow.
The deliberately unprotected switching law is simulation-only and shall not operate physical refrigeration equipment.

baseline.limitation: Manual observation from Lesson 1 cannot regulate temperature after an unplanned load change.

change.decision: Command 100% cooling when PV is at or above SP and 0% otherwise.

disturbances: The door opens at 60 s and closes at 90 s
A focused native test alternates small measurement crossings around SP

acceptance.window: eight controlled measurement-noise crossings with constant underlying temperature

abortPredicates: PV leaves the declared -10 to 10 degC lesson abort range
safety.restorationMode: Auto disabled with compressor demand at 0%
simulationOnlyRestrictions: Single-threshold chatter is intentionally unsafe for physical compressor operation.

video.viewerOutcome: Explain the Boolean control direction, intended temperature cycling, and why noisy threshold crossings damage equipment.

learning.context: Lesson 1 identified the loop but manual observation could not regulate a door disturbance.
learning.reason: A binary compressor needs the simplest automatic feedback law before its limitations can be observed honestly.
theory: ON/OFF control selects one of two actuator states from a Boolean comparison.
Because refrigeration has negative process gain, cooling must turn on when PV is at or above the temperature SP.
A binary actuator produces a temperature cycle rather than convergence to one exact value.
Switching frequency measures how often the actuator changes state; noise near one threshold can make it chatter.
learning.workedPrediction: At a constant 2.00 degC underlying temperature, eight declared measurement-noise values create alternating measured PV samples that command 100, 0, 100, 0, 100, 0, 100, and 0%, creating seven transitions.
practicalPreparation: Predict the control direction and truth table before enabling Auto.
Keep the same plant, 4.00 degC initial state, 60 to 90 s door event, -10 to 10 degC abort range, and seed 20260828 as Lesson 1.
learning.baseline: Recall that a fixed manual command cannot reject the door load.
learning.change: Enable the single-threshold law and run both the door event and the alternating-crossing experiment.
learning.comparison: Compare Lesson 1 manual drift with automatic temperature cycling, then calculate range, switch count, switching frequency, and the seven transitions from eight small threshold crossings.
learning.validation: Qualify the run before using its metrics; verify binary MV, the -10 to 10 degC abort range, the separate 3 degC door-event performance criterion, isolated measurement-noise chatter, and explicit disabled safe restoration.
learning.explanation: Explain why regulation of a band and equipment-friendly switching are different requirements.
learning.transfer: Name another binary actuator where one threshold would regulate the process but excessive switching would be unacceptable.
